method: Components are catalog tools that implement a surface from changes.json directly: ledger codecs, node-to-client clients, chain indexers and query services, nodes, script toolchains, transaction builders, hardware signing and devnet tooling.

Each repository was cloned at its default-branch head (observed.revision) and searched case-insensitively for Dijkstra; GitHub issues and pull requests mentioning Dijkstra were retrieved the same day.
Node-to-client readiness is whether the client offers V23 (wire value 32791), the only version ouroboros-consensus 5.1.0.1 accepts.

Codec readiness is compared with the target ledger CDDL (cardano-ledger 54e24ba4) after removing comments and whitespace; Haskell consumers are compared through the cardano-ledger-dijkstra version their CHaP index-state or constraints select.
Status is per surface group; a component is only as ready as its worst assessment. no-evidence is never a pass.

firstReleases names, per release line, the earliest tag whose source contains every cited source quote (for gouroboros ledger types: the earliest tag whose vendored Dijkstra CDDL is identical to the one compared with the target; for plutus-ledger-api: the target component-set version). Consumer pins are judged only against firstReleases.

in-progress needs visible work toward the target definitions (a branch, an open pull request, or unreleased code on the default branch). A release built only against superseded Dijkstra definitions, with no such work, is a gap.

R4: a devnet result can back an assessment as evidence of kind devnet, naming the check in devnet.json and the version exercised. verified needs a passing result; a failing result cannot back released or verified. Where the target CDDL and the node disagree, the node at the integration revision decides: its Dijkstra header is the ten-field Praos header (devnet check block-shape).

Blockfrost is one component (owner decision, 2026-10-22): its source is the run-your-own backend, which the hosted API runs, so hosted and self-hosted consumers share its statuses. Maestro is deprecated and is not a component; the classification treats a shipped call to it as a gap.

assessments.summary: The language enum stops at PlutusV3, so cost models and witnesses for PlutusV4 (language 3) cannot be represented or decoded.

The transaction body decoder handles keys up to 22 and rejects any other key, so bodies with sub-transactions, guards or account keys (23-27) fail to decode. On the devnet plain Dijkstra transactions decode, but Transaction re-encodes them in the legacy four-element form.

Blocks are decoded in the segregated form (header, transaction bodies, witness sets, auxiliary data, invalid transactions); Dijkstra's [header, block_body] does not match. On the devnet neither 17.0.0 nor 15.0.3 decodes any Dijkstra block.
Protocol parameter updates decode keys up to 33 and reject any other key, so updates of the Dijkstra parameters (34-56) fail.
A pool registration certificate must have exactly ten elements; one carrying Dijkstra's optional BLS key is rejected.

No Dijkstra reference at the observed revision (case-insensitive search of tracked files, lockfiles excluded) and no issue or pull request mentioning Dijkstra. CSL has no era tag of its own, and its builder does not model the Dijkstra rules.

The transaction body ends at key 22 (donation); Dijkstra adds body keys 23-27 (sub-transactions, required guards, direct deposits, balance intervals) and redefines key 14 as guards, so CML cannot decode transactions that use them. On the devnet it rejects every three-element Dijkstra transaction, even plain payments (cml-decoding).
